title: LIVE UPDATES: Impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte
summary: Bookmark this page for Rappler's comprehensive coverage of Vice President Sara Duterte's impeachment trial at the Senate

blocks.text: The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte — the first Philippine public official to be impeached twice by the House of Representatives — began at 2 pm on Monday, July 6.

There are four articles of impeachment against Duterte involving alleged misuse of confidential funds, unexplained wealth, bribery of Department of Education officials, and grave threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and his family.

Only 21 out of 24 senator-judges are physically present. Senator Bato dela Rosa remains in hiding as he faces an International Criminal Court arrest warrant over Rodrigo Duterte’s drug war, Senator Jinggoy Estrada has been detained and suspended in connection with a plunder case, and Senator Rodante Marcoleta surrendered to authorities as he also faces a plunder case.
On this page, we bring you the latest updates, analyses, videos, and photos as the trial of the Vice President unfolds.

blocks.text: LATEST UPDATES
18 minutes ago
Baste Duterte yet to say if he would appear at impeachment trial today
The Senate impeachment court has subpoenaed Davao City Mayor Baste Duterte from Monday, September 28, to Wednesday, September 30, 2026.
However, Senate Sergeant-at-Arms Alfred Corpuz says Duterte did not inform the court if he would appear at the trial on Monday.
Corpuz also says there will be no changes in the security protocols in the Senate.
Duterte was issued with a subpoena to testify in the impeachment trial of his older sister, Vice President Sara Duterte.

blocks.text: Sep 24, 2026 9:30 AM PHT
Rappler Recap: Senate lowers Sara Duterte conviction threshold; minority senators skip vote

The Senate impeachment court on Wednesday, September 23, votes 13-1 to lower the voting threshold for convicting Vice President Sara Duterte, with six senator-judges not participating in the vote. The court says the new computation will exclude members legally or factually unable to participate in the trial.
Multimedia reporter Sandy Locus reports on the vote, the minority senators’ decision not to participate, and Senator Mark Villar’s vote in favor of the appeal.

blocks.text: Sep 24, 2026 8:30 AM PHT
Rappler Recap: How lower conviction threshold changes the math in Sara Duterte’s trial

The Senate impeachment court on Wednesday, September 23, lowers the voting threshold for conviction in Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial, changing the number of votes needed based on the senator-judges eligible to participate in the proceedings.
Rappler multimedia reporter Dwight de Leon explains how the ruling could affect the prosecution and defense, the possible new conviction threshold, and how both sides reacted to the decision.

blocks.text: Sep 23, 2026 9:07 PM PHT
Litigator counters Poa’s argument against lowering voting threshold

“Moving the threshold in terms of impeachment because it serves accountability does not have to mean moving the threshold elsewhere — bogeyman ‘yun,” litigator and Free Legal Assistance member Raffy Aquino said in a Rappler panel discussion during Day 29 of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial on Wednesday, September 23.

The comment was made following defense lawyer Michael Poa’s argument that lowering the voting threshold for impeachment could have consequences on other constitutional provisions, such as revoking or extending martial law, expulsion of a member of the Senate, or amending the Constitution itself. – Rhen Peñada
Sep 23, 2026 8:54 PM PHT
A Villar split: Why is Mark Villar breaking ranks with sister Camille?
Two roads diverged in the Senate on Wednesday, September 23 — and the Villar siblings took different ones.

Senator-judge Mark Villar broke ranks with his sister, Senator-judge Camille Villar, and the Senate minority bloc in a surprise vote on two key motions during the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.
Sep 23, 2026 7:36 PM PHT
Change in voting threshold not yet a ‘justiciable controversy’

Litigator and Free Legal Assistance Group member Raffy Aquino stressed on Wednesday, September 23, that the change in the voting threshold for the impeachment trial does not yet present a “justiciable controversy” that could be reviewed by the Supreme Court (SC).
“There is no injury yet. The Vice President still remains as vice president. And there is no vote yet on the conviction or acquittal,” he explained.
Aquino added that while the SC’s power of judicial review has been expanded to preserve its checking function, it remains limited and requires an actual controversy and grave abuse of discretion.
He added that if the previous threshold of 16 votes is still met, “then there is no controversy” since the conviction would stand.

Based on his experience as an “occasional constitutional litigator,” Aquino said the SC “does not easily lend itself to obstructions,” emphasizing that there must first be an actual controversy before the Court could intervene. – Rena Eñano
Sep 23, 2026 6:14 PM PHT
Why did Mark Villar vote differently from sister Camille?

Following the Senate impeachment court vote on the conviction voting threshold, litigator Raffy Aquino says on Wednesday, September 23, that the Villar siblings Mark and Camille showed one of two things: they either “demonstrated how it is to vote according to one’s conscience,” or it was a strategy to have a foot on either side of the door.

blocks.text: Sep 23, 2026 5:27 PM PHT
Senate court ruling ‘unfavorable’ to Filipinos — Sara Duterte spox
Lawyer Paolo Panelo, spokesperson of Vice President Sara Duterte, says the Senate ruling lowering the cinviction vote threshold was “unfavorable” to the public.

Panelo says, “I don’t think it’s just unfavorable to the VP but to all Filipinos. Binago nila ang Saligang Batas. Hindi ito ang nasa batas natin. Ang nasa batas natin 2/3 of all members, klaro po ‘yun.”
